title: Statcast Bat Tracking — official metric documentation
population: MLB tracked swings; the course uses separate synthetic local testing examples.
access: Public text verified October 13, 2026; introductory definitions and glossary reviewed. No player dataset downloaded.
findings: Documents bat measurement location and swing-selection conventions.
limitations: The main introduction gives a more detailed competitive-swing rule than the page footer. The course does not implement that statistic or equate a local sensor mean with it. Documentation does not establish independent accuracy, training efficacy or an injury threshold.
locations: Bat Tracking Leaderboard, opening definitions (bat location and competitive swings).
Page glossary: exit velocity and bat-tracking definitions; definitions only, no source visual reproduced.

title: A Story of Sprint Speed and Burst — official baseball running explanation
population: Selected MLB running observations from 2017; no training intervention.

findings: Illustrates that different components of a run to first base can produce different comparisons.

title: Hamstring Injury Trends in Major and Minor League Baseball: Epidemiological Findings From the Major League Baseball Health and Injury Tracking System
authors: Okoroha KR, Conte S, Makhni EC, Lizzio VA, Camp CL, Li B, Ahmad CS
type: Descriptive epidemiology study using prospectively recorded surveillance data
population: MLB and MiLB hamstring injuries recorded during 2011–2016.
access: PubMed abstract verified 2026-10-13; indexed official PMC Results and Discussion excerpts reviewed. Direct PMC full-text retrieval returned CAPTCHA and the publisher retrieval failed. Not catalogued as fully reviewed text.
findings: Base running was a common injury context; recurrent injuries were recorded and associated with more time lost than first injuries.
limitations: Historical observational surveillance cannot determine individual readiness, why a particular recurrence occurred, or the effect of a proposed rehabilitation intervention. Detailed methods and tables are not relied upon here.
locations: PubMed abstract: Methods, Results and Conclusion
Indexed PMC Results: Activity; Discussion (context only)
license: Article at DOI 10.1177/2325967119861064. Link and use original limited summaries; no figures, tables or full text redistributed.

title: Hamstring Strain Injury Prevention: Current Beliefs and Practices of Practitioners Working in Major League Baseball
authors: Lazarczuk SL, Headrick J, Hickey JT, Timmins RG, Leva FA, Bourne MN
population: 91 responding practitioners from 28 MLB organizations; survey administered during the 2021 season.
access: Full article PDF available and reviewed at the Maynooth University institutional repository on 2026-10-13. DOI 10.4085/1062-6050-0640.22; direct PMC page returned CAPTCHA.
findings: Respondents identified internal communication and implementation barriers such as scheduling and buy-in. Strategies valued by respondents and those used most often did not fully align.
limitations: Self-report, differing response counts and voluntary participation; beliefs are not causal risk factors or evidence of an intervention’s effectiveness. Practice may have changed since the 2021 survey.
locations: Methods: Data Collection; Data Processing and Analysis
Discussion: Extrinsic Risk Factors; Prevention Strategies
